gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many stops the shopper actually needs. For 24p video at 1/50 s in direct sun at ISO 100 (sunny-16 baseline), that is about 5 stops at f/4, 6 at f/2.8 and 7.3 at f/1.8. A 1–5 stop ND2-32 variable ND therefore can't open up wider than f/4 in sun, while a 1–9 stop ND2-400 reaches f/1.2 and costs $8.89 per stop against $20.70.
standout_why: ChatGPT's search returned no result pages and cited no rivals. Its answer only names ND8, ND64 and ND1000 and explains fixed vs. variable. It gives no stop count tied to aperture, shutter or light, no maximum usable aperture for any filter, and no prices or cost per stop. Rival pages to compare against: none. Its own answer was the only text available.
decides: This changes the pick for the most common video use. Dealectric's listed K&F ND2-32 True Color (67 mm or 77 mm) only works in bright sun at f/4 or narrower at 1/50 s and ISO 100. Shoppers with f/2.8 zooms or f/1.8 primes need the K&F ND2-400 (1–9 stops), which also costs less ($79.99 vs $103.49). Keep the ND2-32 for f/4 zooms, or for people who care most about colour and reflection (0.1% vs 0.2%). Log profiles with a higher minimum ISO push the need further toward the ND2-400.

unsourced: Minimum ISO for Sony S-Log3, such as 800 on the FX3, A7 IV or A7S III, which would add about 3 stops to every figure above. Sony support article 00146206 returned 403 on sony.ca, sony-mea, sony.com.au and sony.ie. The A7S III and FX3 help guide pages on manualslib say only that the ISO range changes with Gamma and that Cine EI has two Base ISOs, with no numbers. The xdcam-user (Alister Chapman) base-ISO chart returned 403, and the LensRentals FX3 PDF wasn't readable. The 800/12800 figure appeared only in search snippets and forums.
